content: Never commit Python cache files (__pycache__) to version control — add __pycache__/ to .gitignore and remove these files from the repository
Never use CORS allow_origins=['*'] in production code — make CORS configuration environment-dependent with specific origins for security
Make hardcoded business values configurable through constants or environment variables — avoid magic numbers like ticket prices, cache TTL, and rates embedded in code
Make database URLs configurable via environment variables — avoid hardcoded database connection strings for different environments (dev/test/prod)
Test public interface methods rather than private methods — avoid testing private methods like _validate_venue_data() directly and instead test the public methods that use them
Remove unused imports to maintain clean code — importing modules when validation is implemented as standalone methods violates code conventions
Use request body with proper schema instead of query parameters for POST endpoints
Validate data integrity constraints at the model level — enforce business rules like preventing negative durations, ensuring end_date is after start_date, and implementing proper field validation
Add business rule validation beyond basic schema validation — missing input validation for duplicate venues, capacity limits, and other business constraints
Implement comprehensive test coverage for all CRUD operations — missing test classes for POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints leaves create, update, and delete operations untested
Use in-memory or shared test databases with proper cleanup instead of separate database files — creating separate test database files causes test isolation issues
Implement proper format validation for structured data fields — zip_code validator should use regex pattern like '^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$' and websites should use HttpUrl type
Whitelist allowed fields or use proper schema for update operations — using hasattr() check without validating against dangerous fields like 'id' creates security risks
Always verify all imported modules and dependencies exist before referencing them — missing files like database.py, models.py, schemas.py cause critical import errors and application failures
Never submit PRs with incomplete/truncated files or failing tests — complete all functions and test implementations and ensure they pass before requesting review
Always ensure database migration enum values match model definitions exactly — migration used 'PLANNING' but model used 'planning', causing runtime failures
Use proper foreign key relationships in tests instead of hardcoded IDs — hardcoded values like venue_id=1, concert_id=1 don't test actual relationships and will fail with real database constraints
Always implement CSRF protection and XSS escaping when using HTMX forms — use Flask-WTF CSRF tokens on data-modifying endpoints (hx-post, hx-delete) and escape user content with {{ content|e }}

Mock chained method calls require explicit return_value assignment at each level — use mock_db.query.return_value.filter.return_value.first.return_value instead of mock_db.query().filter().first.return_value
Never manually manage database sessions by calling next(get_db()) and db.close() — use FastAPI dependency injection or proper session context management instead
Never mix framework-specific syntax between different frameworks — using Flask url_for() in FastAPI templates causes incompatibility errors
Use proper SQLAlchemy 2.0 session patterns in tests with contextlib.contextmanager — avoid manual session management with try/except StopIteration handling
Always call database initialization functions or document their usage — create_tables() function was defined but never called, leaving database tables uncreated

Quality gate 'coverage' has failed repeatedly (percent 0.0 vs threshold 70) across every observed cycle from 2026-04-16 through 2026-08-05 — this is a persistent, unresolved blocker, not a one-off failure

Coverage stuck at 0% while unit_tests pass points to coverage instrumentation (e.g. pytest-cov) not being wired into the test run/report step, rather than tests being absent — fix the coverage tooling config, not just add more tests

Cycles with the coverage quality gate stuck failing at 0% correlate with zero PRs opened and zero PRs merged — the unresolved coverage instrumentation issue may be blocking the pipeline from producing any PR output at all, not just failing a gate after the fact
Never remove essential dependencies that are still in use — pytest, pydantic, alembic, aiosqlite, httpx are needed for testing, schemas, database operations, and FastAPI TestClient imports
Use modern SQLAlchemy 2.0 syntax — DeclarativeBase instead of declarative_base(), .where() instead of .filter() on count() results
Use FastAPI lifespan context manager instead of deprecated @app.on_event('startup') for FastAPI 0.104.1+
Use SQLAlchemy's Enum type for proper database constraints instead of String — storing enum values as strings without database-level enum constraints reduces data integrity
Use Pydantic v2 syntax with `from_attributes = True` and `.model_dump()` instead of deprecated `orm_mode = True` and `.dict()` methods
Never enable SQL logging in production code — using echo=True in SQLAlchemy engine logs all SQL statements to console and should be configurable via environment variables

Never change frameworks without implementing the complete backend infrastructure — switching from FastAPI to Flask requires implementing all routes, models, and app setup before templates can function
Always implement pagination on collection GET endpoints — missing limit/offset parameters causes performance issues with large datasets
Implement foundational layers before dependent components — create models, services, and backend endpoints before writing tests or frontend code that depends on them
Avoid circular imports by placing shared Base classes in a separate module like models/base.py rather than locally — local definitions cause import issues when other models need the same Base
Always include referenced template files in PRs when implementing routes — referencing templates without including them breaks the application
API endpoints should return JSON data following REST conventions — returning raw HTML from API endpoints violates standards and makes testing/maintenance difficult
Integrate validation methods into models or remove them — defining validation methods without connecting them via SQLAlchemy's @validates decorator creates dead code
Implement proper error handling for external dependencies — service methods should handle database connection failures and query timeouts gracefully with appropriate fallback responses
Always implement comprehensive test coverage including dedicated unit tests for service layer business logic — endpoint tests alone are insufficient

e2e_tests and security quality gates are configured as not_run (not pass/fail) every cycle — only unit_tests and coverage actually execute. These suites need to be implemented and wired into the pipeline before they can gate anything

e2e_tests quality gate flipped from its usual 'not_run' status to a failing 'fail' status this cycle, contradicting the prior pattern where e2e_tests and security were both consistently not_run — indicates e2e tests are now being executed (possibly newly wired into CI) and are actively failing, not just skipped.

A cycle can complete with very low cost (~$0.41) and zero PRs opened/merged while unit_tests pass but coverage and e2e_tests both fail — suggests the agent halts early (likely blocked by the persistent 0% coverage gate) before attempting any implementation or PR work, rather than spending budget on a failed attempt.

PRs #191 and #192 were both submitted with self-reported failing/incomplete tests in the PR description (e.g. 'Some tests failing — needs review'). This is a repeated convention violation, not a one-off — PRs must not be opened until tests pass.

PR #192's entire changeset was a binary test.db-journal (SQLite rollback journal) artifact with none of the described functionality (dashboard stats, tour overview, calendar grid endpoints) actually implemented — PR descriptions can claim work that isn't in the diff, so verify diff contents match the description, not just the description itself.
SQLite transient artifacts (*.db, *.db-journal, *.sqlite-journal) are being committed to version control instead of gitignored — add these patterns to .gitignore to prevent recurrence.

Changing SQLALCHEMY_TEST_DATABASE_URL from a file-based sqlite DB to sqlite:// (in-memory) with StaticPool is a global test-infrastructure change affecting every test in the suite — such changes need explicit review of test isolation/ordering, not just a config tweak.

Wrapping the `client` fixture's TestClient in a `with` block triggers FastAPI lifespan startup/shutdown events on every test that uses it — if any setup/teardown logic assumes lifespan doesn't run per-test, this silently breaks state assumptions across the suite.

Never open a PR with known failing tests or a description like 'Some tests failing — needs review.' Identify and fix failing tests before submitting; if a test can't be fixed, investigate and resolve the root cause rather than deferring it to reviewers.

When adding tests/fixtures for a new feature, scope database/config changes narrowly. Reviewer flagged that switching SQLALCHEMY_TEST_DATABASE_URL from a file-based sqlite DB to 'sqlite://' with StaticPool was applied globally, silently changing behavior for every existing test rather than just the new dashboard fixtures — justify and isolate such infra changes, or apply them only to the tests that need them.

When modifying shared test fixtures (e.g. wrapping TestClient in a `with` block to trigger FastAPI lifespan events), check interactions with other autouse fixtures like setup_database before merging — reviewer noted this could cause double-setup or ordering issues across the whole suite.

Never commit transient test/database artifacts (e.g. test.db-journal, *.db, *.sqlite-journal) to version control — add them to .gitignore. PR #192 committed a binary SQLite rollback journal as its entire changeset.

Do not open or submit a PR that claims to close an issue when the actual described functionality (e.g. endpoints, models, templates) is not implemented — verify the diff contains real implementation code, not just artifacts, before submitting. This reinforces prior observed pattern of cycles completing with zero real work but reported as done.

Do not submit PRs with self-reported failing/incomplete tests ('needs review') — per project convention, only submit PRs once tests pass; this matches the recurring pattern of e2e_tests and coverage quality gates failing (0% coverage, 0 passed tests) across cycles.
